To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution of the zeros of the overall impulse response is a function of the correlation between the taps and the distribution of the tap power.
the zeros of mobile radio channels have a distribution that is similar to that of the zeros of random Gaussian polynomials, and this distribution is relevant for the equalizer design.

the density of zeros for the overall transfer function is a function of the correlation of taps of the overall impulse response, and that for uncorrelated taps the density of zeros is proportional to the density of the tap varainces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical distribution of the zeros of a mobile channel.
the statistical properties of the overall transfer functions of mobile channels, with the aim to use the results obtained to improve the design of suboptimally equalized ISI channels.
the statistics of the zeros and poles of the discrete-time transfer function of mobile radio channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distribution of the zeros of the channel is very important for the equalizer design.
the zeros are distributed over the complex unit circle with a density that increases with increasing distance from the unit circle, i.e. the density is maximal at the unit circle.
the distribution of zeros is not a very good indicator for the performance of the receiver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the statistical distribution of zeros of a channel is a powerful tool for the analysis and design of equalizer structures.
we can derive a closed-form expression for the probability density of zeros of mobile radio channels, and that this density is a function of the channel model and the channel parameters.
we are now able to design a suboptimum equalizer for GSM/EDGE channels which is based on a statistical analysis of the mobile channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the zeros of the mobile channels can be well approximated by the zeros of the corresponding random polynomial model.
the density of zeros is not only relevant to the design of sub-optimum equalizers, but also to the design of the channel models.
, in the case of a zero mean tap process, the zeros of a mobile channel transfer function are distributed according to a uniform density on the unit circle.
